cases.reason: GR3 executes 'the COMPUTE statement defined in general rule 2' before the line prints, and that COMPUTE is evaluated under the source element's ARITHMETIC mode. 2002 has ARITHMETIC IS STANDARD (11.8.4). Under it, every operation's result is truncated to 32 significant digits (8.8.1.3.2, 8.8.1.3.1.1). 2023 has no STANDARD phrase, only NATIVE, STANDARD-BINARY and STANDARD-DECIMAL (11.9.5). So in 2002, GR3 also governs an implicit COMPUTE in standard arithmetic, a mode the 2023 row cannot show. The row's witnesses (pb1292_source_forms_85, pb1294_*) run in native arithmetic only. Probe source_std_2002.cob (OPTIONS ARITHMETIC IS STANDARD; A PIC 9(21) = 10**20; B = 10**-12; SOURCE A + B - A into PIC 9.9(12)) at --std 2002. The 2002 text requires 0.000000000000: A + B needs 33 digits and is truncated to A. The compiler prints R=0.000000000001, and the same value for the control COMPUTE W = A + B - A. WRONG: this is the known 32-versus-34-digit standard-arithmetic defect, reaching this rule through the implicit COMPUTE. needs: its own verdict. The compiler at --std 2002 evaluates a SOURCE arithmetic expression under ARITHMETIC IS STANDARD with more than 32 digits. compiler-at-2002: wrong.

cases.reason: GR4 acts on 'the associated size error indicator', which GR1 and GR3 define, and in 2002 GR4 is the ONLY point where EC-REPORT-SUM-SIZE is set. 2002 GR3: a size error in an addition only sets the indicator. 2023 GR3 changed this: the condition is set at the addition itself. So in 2002, with EC-REPORT-SUM-SIZE checking on, a program runs on past the overflowing GENERATE and takes the fatal condition when the counter is presented (GR4). The row's witness pb1130_report_sum_size_line_overlap runs with checking off, so it never shows this arm. Probe sum_ec_2002.cob (>>TURN EC-REPORT-SUM-SIZE CHECKING ON; PIC 9 counter; GENERATE 5, then GENERATE 6, each followed by a DISPLAY; then TERMINATE) at --std 2002. The 2002 text requires AFTER-GEN-1, AFTER-GEN-2, then termination at TERMINATE. The compiler prints AFTER-GEN-1, then 'abnormal run-unit termination: EC-REPORT-SUM-SIZE ... an addition into sum counter 1 is a size error (ISO §2023:13.18.54.4 GR3)' at the second GENERATE, the same as at --std 2023. WRONG at 2002: GR4's raise is never reached, and 2023's GR3 raise fires instead. A second difference in GR4's own text: 2023 GR4 adds the ROUNDED sentence. 2002's SUM format carries [ROUNDED], but 2002 GR4 and GR3 compute the counter by plain ADD with ON SIZE ERROR. The compiler applies the SUM rounded-phrase to every addition (ReportWriterEmitter.SumAddition, sum.Rounding) at every edition. The reader's 'no-op at the move' argument does not cover that. needs: its own verdict. At --std 2002 EC-REPORT-SUM-SIZE is raised at presentation and not at addition; sum_ec_2002.cob is the witness once fixed. compiler-at-2002: wrong.
